key_insight: Al-Ghasali models closed, finite propositional Fiqh rule systems as deterministic finite-state automata, with LLMs restricted to expressing their outputs.
engineering_relevance: The framework offers a formally constrained architecture for rule-based decision support, claiming O(1) verdict extraction after offline compilation.
method: Compile finite propositional Horn rules into deterministic automata, including hierarchical subchapters and order-sensitive states.
Generate unambiguous right-linear output grammars from automaton execution histories.
Constrain LLM decoding with these grammars, a bounded neutral lexicon, and valence locking.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports formal proofs of complexity and hallucination-prevention guarantees under stated design conditions, but no datasets, benchmarks, or empirical evaluations.
watch_item: The guarantees depend on faithful rule formalization and enforced output constraints; compilation cost and state-space growth still require practical evaluation.
paper_title: Al-Ghasali: A Computational Framework for Simulating Islamic Jurisprudential Rulings via Finite State Automata and Large Language Models
